<x_0.1309><y_0.0641>a great height; to accomplish which, they climb up some eminence, and are walked about by the winds, filling the air with their threads. They are destroyed by the spikes and ichneumon.<x_0.5146><y_0.1234><class_Text>

<x_0.1338><y_0.1172>Linnaeus has subdivided this genus according to the number and position of their eyes:<x_0.5156><y_0.1508><class_Text>

<x_0.2705><y_0.1531>**A.** _Eyes eight._<x_0.376><y_0.1719><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2402><y_0.175>_1. Eyes placed thus_, :<x_0.4121><y_0.1922><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0586><y_0.1953>fasnata. Of a silver color; the abdomen marked with yel- lowish bandes; the legs surrounded with brown rings. 49. A native of the island of Malachi<x_0.5176><y_0.2367><class_List-item>

<x_0.0605><y_0.2352>* diadema Abdomen nearly globale and reddish; brown, mark- ed with a white cross composed of dots. 1. A native of Europe, on trees; it is a very beautiful insect.<x_0.5195><y_0.2797><class_List-item>

<x_0.0615><y_0.2742>_aquatica_ Browny abbonen ovat and of an ash colour; the back brown, marked with two dots. 30. A native of Europe, in stagnant waters, where it direct to the bottom in search of the area. It takes up to winter quar-ters in an empty snail shell, the aperture of which it closes up with a web; jaws black, claws red.<x_0.5234><y_0.3609><class_List-item>

<x_0.0625><y_0.3836>_latro._<x_0.0859><y_0.3828><class_Text>

<x_0.1348><y_0.382>Thorax hairy, and of an ash colour; the abdomen oval, black, and spotted with red. 95. A native of America; large, the thorax oval, legs black, thighs pale.<x_0.5205><y_0.4367><class_List-item>

<x_0.1416><y_0.5453>99. A native of Europe, in meadows.<x_0.4111><y_0.5617><class_List-item>

<x_0.0664><y_0.5961>_argentata._<x_0.1436><y_0.5938><class_Text>

<x_0.1387><y_0.5945>Abdown white, and brown behind, and marked round the edge with six small projections. 70. A native of South America.<x_0.5244><y_0.6406><class_Text>

<x_0.0674><y_0.6719>fumigate.<x_0.1426><y_0.6922><class_Text>

<x_0.1396><y_0.668>Abdenom oval and brown, marked at the base with two white dots. 16. A native of Europe, in meadows; it washes near the nest of the larva of different insects, and make their coming out, when it leaves on one after another, and sucks out their substance.<x_0.5254><y_0.7398><class_List-item>

<x_0.0684><y_0.7414>_saccata._<x_0.1445><y_0.7711><class_Text>

<x_0.1406><y_0.7383>Abdomoval, of a brownial, colour, 40. A native of Europe, age gardens, and carries its eggs behind it enclosed in a bag; legs livid, marked with unequal brown rings set close together.<x_0.5293><y_0.7969><class_List-item>

<x_0.2764><y_0.7984>_Eyes placed thus, :_<x_0.4131><y_0.8141><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0703><y_0.8211>_extensa._<x_0.1318><y_0.8352><class_Text>

<x_0.1377><y_0.8156>Abdemon long, of a silver colour tinged with green, the legs extended longitudinally. 22. A native of Europe, in woods; its legs are applied closely to the branches.<x_0.5303><y_0.8719><class_List-item>

<x_0.0723><y_0.8727>_ridulana._<x_0.1328><y_0.8859><class_Text>

<x_0.0752><y_0.8742>_Shining black; the abdomen hairy and black. 73._ A native of America; it forms a nest under ground, and spin as large cylindrical web, which is covered with a id; its bite is very painful, and frequently oc- casions fever and delirium, which is soon removed by a<x_0.5283><y_0.9437><class_List-item>

<x_0.5312><y_0.057>gentle suborfics, thorax marked with a large depressed circular spot; abdominal oval; legs equal.<x_0.9131><y_0.0883><class_Text>

<x_0.5459><y_0.1133>Black, thorax marked with a white line on the back\* density 79. A native of Britain.<x_0.9756><y_0.1461><class_Text>

<x_0.5332><y_0.1422>Marked with triangular black spots on the back of torantsis, the abdomen; the legs spotted with black. 34. A native of the south of Europe, particularly Italy and Barbary. It is found in screens in agriculture soil; its bite was formerly supposed to be combble by nothing but remains; though it occasions a great deal of pain, it is almost never fatal.<x_0.9746><y_0.2391><class_Text>

<x_0.6436><y_0.2422>## 8. Eyes placed thus,<x_0.8262><y_0.2625><class_Section-header>

<x_0.5352><y_0.2664>Oval and oblong; thorax hair, white; abdomen and _pakkra_. legs black, marked with yellow bands. 32. A native of Europe.<x_0.9736><y_0.3125><class_Text>

<x_0.5371><y_0.3531>Black, abdominal oval, forehead white, and leaps on gocuit, its prey. 84. It is to be found frequently in woods about Vienna; abdommed with two compressed dots.<x_0.9639><y_0.4102><class_Text>

<x_0.6406><y_0.4109>## 10. Eyes placed thus,<x_0.8213><y_0.4281><class_Section-header>

<x_0.5381><y_0.4344>Thorax orbicular and convex, with a transverse cen-orientral tra excavation. 31. It is a native of South America, among others, where a preys upon the larger insects, and even small birds, dropping into their nests, and sucking their blood and legs; it is of so enormous a size, that its flag may be compared to the latons of a havk, and its eyes are very large.<x_0.9766><y_0.5352><class_Text>

<x_0.54><y_0.5742>Of a grayish rusty colour, and slightly clouded; tho-truncets, rax globular, and slightly heart-shaped; abdomen some-what irregular, and marked with a faint longitudinal cross. 85. A native of Europe, on oak and other trees; abdommed marked with four impressed dots on the back; papilla three.<x_0.9785><y_0.657><class_Text>

Tho-rax buck, slightly tinged with rusty colour, and nearly double behind; legs gravy, marked with brown rings; abdommed marked as a whilish spot; beneath resem- bhing a horse shoe; papilla four.<x_0.9707><y_0.8227><class_Text>
